Procedural timing; affects when amount becomes known, not a direct cash item.
Single motion (D.I. 611) stating one requested relief: the grounds and the resulting requested amount are one request; splitting would separate the amount from its basis.

Entity scope ambiguous; re-propose with target naming both movant defendants and the motion itself.

findings.proposition: Akoustis reported approximately $15.2 million of cash at 31 March 2024 and substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern; it had only about 3.0 million unissued and unreserved authorized shares after the May 2024 offering, so absent a stockholder-approved increase it is limited to non-equity financing, while the 6.0% notes limit additional debt; it lists the $44.0 million notes and the $4.0 million GDSI promissory note (including potential events of default under them) and the $38.6 million Qorvo judgment among factors limiting its ability to raise capital, and says it may otherwise have to curtail operations or undergo restructuring or insolvency proceedings.
findings.target: Akoustis Technologies, Inc. — liquidity, going-concern status and capacity to raise capital after the Qorvo verdict (424B5 risk factors)
findings.subject: Liquidity and financing capacity

spans.quote: As of March 31, 2024, we had approximately $15.2 million of cash and cash equivalents.
we believe there is substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.
we effectively have 3.0 million available unissued and unreserved authorized shares to meet the needs of our business.

Absent an increase in the shares of common stock authorized for issuance under our Certificate of Incorporation, we will be limited to non-equity financing structures in the event additional financing is required.
Additionally, the terms of our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 impose certain limitations on our ability to incur additional debt obligations.

the amounts outstanding under our $44.0 million principal amount of our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 and a $4.0 million promissory note issued in connection with our acquisition of GDSI (including the potential we may experience one or more defaults or events of default under such instruments); and

the uncertainty that the approximately $38.6 million judgment awarded to Qorvo in the Qorvo Litigation has created regarding our financial condition and prospects and potential negative impact on our ability to raise additional capital.

we may be forced to undertake additional measures, which may include delaying or reducing our R&D plan and/or manufacturing and sales activities, materially curtailing or eliminating our operations, selling or disposing of our rights or assets, pursuing sale or other strategic transactions, or undergoing restructuring or insolvency proceedings.

reconciliations.note: The statements agree: What permanent injunction does Qorvo seek against Akoustis's products or operations, when would it be decided, and could it interrupt Akoustis's product revenue and customer receipts? | No conflict. fnd_016 records what Qorvo asks the court to order (an injunction on the '018/'755 Patent Enjoined Products and not-more-than-colorably-different products, with a 14-day certification requirement for redesigned products). fnd_018 records Akoustis's own claim that its redesigned XBAW products avoid the patents and that it can continue selling notwithstanding an injunction against legacy products. Both stand: they are opposing party positions on a motion not yet decided; whether redesigned products fall outside the injunction is an open unknown (the court has not ruled and Qorvo's proposed order would require Akoustis to certify non-infringement).

The statements agree: What money judgment did the D. Del. court enter against Akoustis in favour of Qorvo, in what amount and on what date, and what post-trial motions (new trial/remittitur, amend judgment, fees, injunction) are pending that could change the amount or timing of payment? | No conflict. fnd_017 is Qorvo's public description of the verdict and its intent to pursue an injunction; fnd_020 records Akoustis's docketed motions challenging that judgment. They concern the same judgment from opposite parties; both stand.

The statements agree: Does the 6.0% convertible notes indenture make an unpaid/unstayed final judgment above a threshold, or a delisting (fundamental change), an event of default or repurchase trigger that could accelerate $44.0M of notes during the Slope installment window? | No conflict. fnd_012 covers the listing Event of Default (7.01(b)) and fundamental-change repurchase (10.01); fnd_022 covers different clauses of the same indenture (7.01(c) interest default, 7.01(h) cross-default, 5.12 liens, 7.01(e) covenant defaults). Both stand as complementary terms of one instrument.
